newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Over two mln IBM shares sold from offshore.
newsitem.headline: Over two mln IBM shares sold from offshore.

text.p: Over two million shares in information technology firm IBM South Africa (IBM SA) were sold into the Johannesburg market from offshore on Thursday morning, depressing the firm's share price, dealers said.

They said the large trade could be linked to a massive asset swap deal carried out on Wednesday by broker SBC Warburg which saw around two billion rand's worth of mainly blue-chip shares move offshore.
"It looks like some of the shares that were sold yesterday are finding their way back into the local market. The deal (on Thursday in IBM SA) was also done by Warburgs," a trader said.
The bulk of the IBM SA shares moved back into South Africa in two separate deals of 736,000 shares each, boosting turnover in the stock to 21.69 million rand by 0930 GMT.
IBM SA, which had last dipped 35 cents to 10.50 rand, was the second most active stock by volume on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange in morning dealings.

The asset swap on Wednesday which dealers said probably represented a portfolio being moved offshore, lifted overall trading value to 2.776 billion rands worth of shares -- beating the previous April 29 record of 2.171 billion rand.
IBM SA in April warned that it expected to show a substantial trading loss for the six months to June 30.
It announced at the same time that it would restructure to improve focus on higher growth areas in a bid to better its competitiveness. Further costs would be associated with the restructure.
